source_resolution.argument: Specializes the exact transformed scalar constraint to flat Euclidean background, K=0, tau=0 and Lambda=0. The base fields are prescribed independently and divergence-free; the actual seed fields are epsilon times the base fields, so their squared source is epsilon^2 S. It defines the bounded smooth Dirichlet problem and explicitly asserts no momentum equation, existence, or global/puncture result.

source_resolution.argument: Defines T_epsilon(x)=x-L^{-1}F(x,epsilon), obtains a uniform contraction on a closed ball from continuity of D_xF, chooses the parameter interval so the map lands strictly inside the ball, invokes the exact complete-metric contraction theorem, proves parameter Lipschitz continuity and nearby invertibility by the Neumann series, and derives the C1 branch formula by difference quotients.

source_dispositions.locator: Chapter XII, Theorem 12.8 and proof, printed pp. 256–259.

source_resolution.argument: For arbitrary f in C0alpha, Poincare and Cauchy–Schwarz make the local weak form bounded and Lax–Milgram gives the unique H0^1 solution of -Delta u=f/8. The exact pinned global Schauder theorem applies with n=3, the bounded C-infinity domain, exponent alpha, right-hand side f/8 and zero trace; the stated AC and Countable Choice assumptions match. The maximum principle proves injectivity. This yields the required isomorphism, but it does not locally reconstruct the design’s requested trace/density, flattening, Newtonian Hölder-kernel, reflection/localization and continuation chain; this route mismatch is escalated.

source_resolution.argument: Proves the C2alpha-to-C0alpha inclusion from finite smooth boundary charts and local path-length control, then proves the C0alpha product estimate, positivity openness, reciprocal/power composition bounds, the exact cubic inverse-power remainder and continuity of the Fréchet derivative.

source_resolution.argument: Defines F(u,epsilon)=(-8Delta)u-2epsilon^2S(1+u)^-3 on the positive open set, verifies its C1 and invertible derivative, obtains the unique local branch, proves psi>=1 by the weak maximum principle, and uses the inverse estimate and cubic Lipschitz remainder to show u=epsilon^2v+O_X(epsilon^4). All conclusions remain local to the fixed bounded Dirichlet problem.

source_resolution.argument: Uses constant base field E0=a e1 and B0=0, whose actual epsilon-scaled fields have zero divergence and source S=a^2. The polynomial v=a^2(R^2-|x|^2)/24 has zero boundary trace and satisfies -8Delta v=2S, so the theorem gives the claimed local branch and remainder.
